why: Each figure has a square with a small triangle on one side and a circle. In every next figure the triangle moves one side clockwise: top, right, bottom, left, so it must go back to the top. The circle sits on the opposite side of the triangle in figures 1 and 3, and on the same side in figures 2 and 4, so it alternates. Figure 5 is an odd step, so the circle is opposite the triangle again, at the bottom. Option 4 fails because its circle is on the same side as the triangle.
trick: Track each part separately: follow the triangle's rotation, then check whether the circle is on the same or the opposite side. Look for an alternating pattern.
note: Option 4 drawn as triangle top with circle top; option 5 triangle bottom with circle top.
